hints.title: Read the circle data
hints.body: Use the completed-square equations to identify both centres and the known radius. Calculate the distance between the centres.
hints.recap: The radius is the positive square root of the squared radius in a circle equation.
hints.pitfall: The signs inside the coordinate brackets are opposite to the corresponding centre coordinates.
hints.pause: Write down the two centres and calculate their separation.

recall.reminder: The radius is the positive square root of the squared radius in a circle equation.

hints.title: Draw both contact arrangements
hints.body: Two circles with exactly one shared point may touch externally or internally. Draw their centres and the contact point on one line.
hints.recap: At external contact the centre distance is the sum of the radii; at internal contact it is their absolute difference.
hints.pitfall: Check positivity of every candidate radius.
hints.pause: Form and solve the two contact equations, then take the difference of the valid radii.

recall.reminder: At external contact the centre distance is the sum of the radii; at internal contact it is their absolute difference.

solution:
The centres are separated by 122+52=13. External tangency gives r+8=13, so r=5. Internal tangency gives |r−8|=13; its only positive solution is r=21.

The difference is 21−5=16.

Answer C: 16.
